target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech companies paying for computational antibody design and modeling
problem: Finding antibodies against hard targets is slow and expensive in the lab; computational design aims to narrow candidates.
business_model: Fee for service project work with possible royalties on commercialized drugs; government grants
product_category: Computational antibody design and drug discovery

founders.name: Monica Berrondo
prior_employers: Trained pharmaceutical employees on academic molecular modeling software (employer not named)
education: PhD (field not stated; chemical engineering and biophysics background per VentureBeat)
founders.background_notes: Company site: scientist and software engineer with more than 10 peer reviewed papers.

founders.name: Susana Kaufmann
prior_employers: Senior developer roles across petrochemical, combustion, pharma and finance; managed a software consulting company (company site)
founders.background_notes: Described as Berrondo's mother by VentureBeat.

competitors.name: Atomwise
competitors.what: AI driven small molecule drug discovery, also a YC graduate

technical_complexity.rationale: Predicting antibody structures and designing binders computationally is research grade; accuracy limited in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary algorithms and antibody database, but pharma buyers can build or buy similar tools and results need lab validation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents absorbing it; AI antibody design later drew many funded entrants (Absci, others) per a review article.

market_need_then: VentureBeat reported customers in the US, UK, Switzerland, Germany and China and secondhand reports of 10 paying customers and $50,000 revenue in 2017.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder recognized as Austin Magazine Woman of the Year 2013 and Austin Startup Week Founder of the Year 2015 (company site); no brand community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Technical B2B name with little brand coverage; mother daughter YC story drew some press.

outcome_analysis: Macromoltek is a long running, small computational antibody design shop that used NSF grants and the YC 120 thousand dollar deal rather than venture rounds. It is still active and now markets AI antibody discovery, but no sizeable equity round, acquisition or breakout customer was found, which points to a service business that stayed small while larger funded AI antibody companies emerged.
notes: YC page says founded 2010, VentureBeat says 2011; 2010 used. VentureBeat says close to $1M in NSF grants; an aggregator lists NSF SBIR award 1632399 of $1,193,494 for 2016 to 2020, unverified, so the grant amount is null. CB Insights lists $370K total, a $250K PPP loan on 2020-05-01 and other investors (Capital Factory, Ataria Ventures); aggregator only, unrecorded. Another profile says $1.49M over four rounds. ACC incubator post (2018-03-05) confirms an NSF SBIR supplement tied to Macromoltek. Only one competitor sourced near batch; directory lists (MAbSilico, Zymeworks, Adagene) are undated and not listed. Name origin not found.
